$comment: What a member menu may offer, read by tests/shared/powers.test.ts and the Android SharedCorpusTest. There is no IRCv3 specification for this: no extension tells a client whether it may kick. ISUPPORT gives the roles a network has (PREFIX) and which modes take a mask (CHANMODES), and the rest is inference — so this errs toward offering something a network might refuse and never toward hiding something it would have allowed, except where there is no rank at all and we can be sure. Ignoring somebody is a decision about your own client rather than the channel and belongs in this menu, but neither client keeps an ignore list yet; it goes in when the list behind it does.
$cases: `mine` and `theirs` are the prefix symbols each person is wearing in the channel. `actions` is the menu, in order.

cases.name: somebody with no rank is offered nothing to do to anybody
cases.$comment: The case that prompted this. Both clients showed Kick to everybody and let the server answer 482, which teaches people that half the menu is a lie.

cases.name: and nothing to do to themselves either
an op gets the lot
taking back what has been given
cases.$comment: Each one reads as its opposite when they already have it, so the menu never offers to give somebody something they have.

cases.name: a halfop may moderate but not appoint
cases.$comment: Where the networks disagree. rIRCd refuses a halfop's kick and InspIRCd allows it; offered, because a network with the role usually means it to moderate, and a refusal costs one line where hiding costs the feature.

cases.name: a voiced user is not staff
nobody acts on somebody standing above them
cases.$comment: The one permission rule every ircd agrees on.

cases.name: an op may act on another op
an owner outranks an op
and is outranked by nobody
cases.$comment: No mute here: on UnrealIRCd `q` is the owner prefix, not a quiet mode, so offering one would be offering to make somebody the owner. The owner rungs used to be missing altogether — an owner's menu stopped at Make operator, so the one person who could hand the channel on had no way to.

cases.name: a network with only ops and voice has no halfop to give
an op can take their own badge off
cases.$comment: Standing down is something you do to yourself, so the rank rule does not block it. Only the taking-off half is offered: giving yourself a badge you lack is something the server refuses, and offering halfop to somebody who is already op is noise.

cases.name: a network that sends no PREFIX still works
cases.$comment: Falling back to the pair every ircd has had since before ISUPPORT existed. No ban, because nothing said there is a ban list.

cases.name: a network with no ban list is not offered one
and an op who is also voiced can take both off
a founder on rIRCd can hand the channel to somebody else
cases.$comment: The whole point of this pass. The menu used to stop at Make operator, so the one person who could pass the channel on had no way to — and /owner sent +q, which on rIRCd is the quiet list, so the command for it silenced them instead.

cases.name: and take it back from somebody who has it
an admin may make another admin but not a founder
and may not touch the founder standing above them
an operator may not hand out admin or founder
a founder standing down is offered only that
cases.$comment: On yourself the only sensible half is giving something up — and only what you are actually wearing. A founder holds `^` and nothing else, so there is one thing to lay down rather than five.

cases.name: the classic ladder spells founder q and it works the same
cases.$comment: No mute: this ladder spends `q` on the owner prefix, so there is no quiet mode left for it to mean.

cases.name: a network with no rungs above operator offers none
nor does one with only ops and voice

$masks: What to ban somebody with. A ban on a nick is undone by changing it, which takes one command and no privileges, so the host is what gets banned when it is known.

masks.name: the host, where it is known
a cloak is still a host

masks.$comment: Weaker, and worth saying so in the menu: one NICK undoes it.
masks.name: the nick, when there is nothing better
an empty host is no host

$roles: Which group a member belongs in and what it is called, read off ISUPPORT rather than assumed. Both clients had the five prefixes of the 1990s written in with nothing for anything else, so rIRCd's ^ for founders fell to rank 0 and into the heading meant for people wearing nothing — and on the desktop that drew two headings both reading "Members".

roles.name: a founder on rIRCd is a founder, not a member
roles.label: Founders

roles.name: an operator, which every server agrees about
roles.label: Operators

roles.name: voice is the bottom rung, not no rung
roles.label: Voiced

roles.name: the classic ladder calls its top mode q, and it is still founders
roles.label: Founders

roles.name: an admin is an admin whichever symbol it wears
roles.label: Admins

roles.name: ops and voice together are ops
roles.label: Operators

roles.name: and in whatever order they arrived
roles.label: Operators

roles.name: a symbol this network does not use is nobody
roles.label: Members

roles.name: a mode with no name is named after itself
roles.label: Mode +z

roles.name: a server that says nothing has ops and voice
roles.label: Operators

roles.name: and on such a server a tilde means nothing
roles.label: Members

$modes: Which mode letter a network uses for a rung. The top one is `q` where a server has it and `x` on rIRCd, which keeps `q` for its quiet list — so a client that assumed `q` promoted people by silencing them.

modes.name: and the admin a, like everybody
the classic ladder calls the founder q
operator is o wherever there is one
a network with no founder has none to name
nor a half-op, on a server with only ops and voice
a top rung nobody has a word for is not a founder
a server that says nothing has ops and voice
